==English== [[File:MDRBobMomSmall.jpg|right|thumb|A woman with two children [[circa|c.]] 1933.]] ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/tʃaɪld/|[tʃaɪ̯ɫd]|[ˈtʃaɪ̯.ɫ̩d]|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-child.ogg|a=GA|IPA=[ˈtʃaɪ̯.ɫ̩d]}} ** {{IPA|en|[tʃəɪ̯(ə)ɫd]|a=CA,dialectal}} ** {{IPA|en|[tʃaːɫd]|a=Southern US}} * {{IPA|en|/tʃɑj(ə)ld/|a=SSB}} ** {{audio|en|en-uk-child.ogg|a=SSB|IPA=/tʃɑjəld/}} * {{IPA|en|/tʃɑeld/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/tʃʌɪld/|a=Scotland}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪld|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|child}} * {{hmp|en|childe}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:child|id=noun|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|child}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ċild}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*kilþ}}, {{m|gmw-pro|*kelþ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*kelþaz||[[womb]]; [[fetus]]}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵelt-||[[womb]]}}, perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gel-||to ball up, amass}}. Cognate with {{cog|da|kuld||[[brood]], [[litter]]}}, {{cog|sv|kull||[[brood]], [[litter]]}}, {{cog|is|kelta}}, {{m|is|kjalta||[[lap]]}}, {{cog|got|𐌺𐌹𐌻𐌸𐌴𐌹||[[womb]]}}, {{cog|sa|जर्त}}, {{m|sa|जर्तु||tr=jártu|[[vulva]]}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|childe||archaic}} * {{alter|en|chile||eye dialect|Southern US}} * {{sense|plural}} {{alter|en|childrens||intentionally incorrect|nonstandard}}; {{alter|en|childs||nonstandard|rare}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|children|childer}} # {{senseid|en|kid aged 0 to 17 years}} {{lb|en|[[Appendix:Glossary#broadly|broadly]]}} A [[person]] who has not yet reached [[adulthood]], whether [[natural]] ([[puberty]]), [[cultural]] ([[initiation]]), or [[legal]] ([[majority]]). #: {{syn|en|kid}} #: {{hypo|en|newborn|neonate|preteen|adolescent|tweenager|teenager|tween|teen|preadult}} #: {{ux|en|Go easy on him: he is but a '''child'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Regular chores can be appropriate for '''children''', given age-appropriate limits on difficulty level and time on task.}} #*: {{quote|en|And not just the '''children''', teenagers too. Chuck wants a football, Kathleen a tattoo.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=w:Joseph Stiglitz|volume=188|issue=26|page=19|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|title=Globalisation is about taxes too|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/may/27/globalisation-is-about-taxes-too|passage=It is time the international community faced the reality: we have an unmanageable, unfair, distortionary global tax regime. {{...}} It is the starving of the public sector which has been pivotal in America no longer being the land of opportunity – with a '''child''''s life prospects more dependent on the income and education of its parents than in other advanced countries.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013204907/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/may/27/globalisation-is-about-taxes-too|archivedate=13 October 2026}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Dakin Andone|title=3 children who are US citizens — including one with cancer — deported with their mothers, lawyers and advocacy groups say|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/04/27/us/children-us-citizens-deported-honduras/index.html|date=2025-04-27|passage=In one case, a mother was deported and took her 2-year-old '''child''' with her, while the other involves another mother deported and her 4- and 7-year-old '''children''' went with her, the American Civil Liberties Union and the National Immigration Project, among other organizations, said in a news release Friday.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830094739/https://www.cnn.com/2025/04/27/us/children-us-citizens-deported-honduras/index.html|archivedate=30 August 2026}} ## {{senseid|en|kid aged 1 to 11 years}} {{lb|en|[[pediatrics]]|sometimes, in a [[Appendix:Glossary#strict|stricter]] sense}} A youth aged 1 to 9 years, whereas [[neonate#Noun|neonates]] are aged 0 to 1 month, [[infant#Noun|infants]] are aged 1 to 12 months, and [[adolescent#Noun|adolescents]] are aged 10 to 20 years. ##: {{hyper|en|kid}} ##: {{cot|en|newborn|neonate|infant|adolescent|teenager|teen|boy|girl}} # {{senseid|en|offspring of any age including adulthood}} {{lb|en|with possessive}} One's [[direct]] [[descendant]] by [[birth]], regardless of [[age]]; one's [[offspring]]; a [[son]] or [[daughter]]. #: {{ux|en|My youngest '''child''' is forty-three this year.}} #: {{ux|en|His adult '''children''' visit him yearly.}} # {{senseid|en|cartomancy}} {{lb|en|cartomancy}} The thirteenth [[Lenormand]] card. # {{senseid|en|figuratively, of times or tribes}} {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[figurative]] [[offspring]], ''particularly:'' ## A person considered a [[product]] of a [[place]] or [[culture]], a [[member]] of a [[tribe]] or culture, regardless of age. ##: {{ux|en|the '''children''' of Israel}} ##: {{ux|en|He is a '''child''' of his times.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=[[w:Edward Plunkett, 18th Baron of Dunsany|Edward John Moreton Dunsany]]|title={{w|The Last Book of Wonder|Tales of Wonder}}|page=64|passage=Plash-Goo was of the '''children''' of the giants, whose sire was Uph. And the lineage of Uph had dwindled in bulk for the last five hundred years, till the giants were now no more than fifteen foot high; but Uph ate elephants{{...}}}} ## {{senseid|en|figuratively, derived or caused}} Anything [[derive]]d from or [[cause]]d by something. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=w:Salman Rushdie| title={{w|Midnight's Children|Midnight's '''Children'''}}| passage=Poverty, disease, and despair are the '''children''' of war.}} ## {{senseid|en|child element in computing}} {{lb|en|computing}} A [[data]] [[item]], [[process]], or [[object]] which has a [[subservient]] or [[derivative]] [[role]] relative to another. ##: {{ux|en|The '''child''' node then stores the actual data of the parent node.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=John Mongan; Noah Kindler; Eric Giguère|title=Programming Interviews Exposed |passage=The algorithm pops the stack to obtain a new current node when there are no more '''children''' (when it reaches a leaf).}} # {{senseid|en|childe, youth of noble birth}} {{alt form|en|childe||youth of noble birth}}. # {{senseid|en|mathematics}} {{lb|en|mathematics|programming}} A subordinate [[node]] of a [[tree]]. # {{lb|en|figurative}} An adult or adolescent with [[childish]] or [[stupid]] behaviors. #: {{usex|en|My husband is such a '''child''', going out with his sled everytime it snows.}} # {{senseid|en|female child, obsoletely}} {{lb|en|obsolete|specifically}} A [[female]] child, a [[girl]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|III|iii|288|2|passage=A boy, or a '''Childe''' I wonder?}} [[procreate]]. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|year=1596.2|book=VI|canto=XII|stanza=17|page=512|passage= My liefe (ſayd ſhe) ye know, that long ygo,

A little mayde, the which ye '''chylded''' tho ;
The ſame againe if now ye liſt to haue,
The ſame is yonder Lady, whom high God did ſaue.}} #* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne|18|stanza=26|320|And from his fertill hollow wombe forth ran,
(Clad in rare weedes and ſtrange habiliment)
A Nymph, for age able to goe to man,

'''Childed''' an hundreth Nymphes, ſo great, ſo dight:{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear Q1|act=III|scene=v|passage={{...}}But then the mind much ſufferance doth or'e ſcip,
When griefe hath mates,​and bearing fellowſhip :
How light and portable my paine ſeemes now,
When that which makes me bend, makes the King bow,
He '''childed''' as I fathered,​''Tom'' away,
